newsitem.title: USA: LightPath Technologies Q4 full results.
newsitem.headline: LightPath Technologies Q4 full results.

text.p: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M., Sept. 6 (Reuter) LightPath Technologies on Friday released results for the fiscal year ending June 30. Full text of release follows.

LightPath Technologies Inc. (symbol - LPTHU Nasdaq, Small Cap Market), producer of GRADIUM(TM) glass lenses for industry, telecommunications, medical applications and research, today reported revenues of $220,444 for the fiscal year ended June 30, an increase of 20 percent over those for the prior fiscal year.
Net loss for fiscal 1996 was $2,914,905 or $1.98 per share, compared with a net loss of $2,789,580 or $3.95 per share for the comparable prior period.
The weighted number of shares outstanding increased some 108 percent as a result of LightPath's February 1996 initial public offering.

Leslie A. Danziger, chairman and chief executive officer, said that LightPath, in the fiscal year just ended, began developing a plan to focus increasingly on marketing to the industrial laser optics market, including the auto industry, and on the application of GRADIUM(TM) glass in technologies that will expand the information-carrying capability of optical fiber used in telecommunications. LightPath also began selling its first line of standard GRADIUM(TM) lenses through print and Internet versions of the first LightPath catalog.

"In the industrial laser market, we believe GRADIUM(TM) lenses' greater focusing power and smaller 'spot size' will provide greater precision and higher productivity on the assembly line," she said. "In telecommunications, we are

positioning GRADIUM(TM) glass as an enabling material for new devices, including one being developed under a Defense Department contract, that would allow a single strand of optical fiber to handle all types of communications, including telephonic, computer, cable TV and high-speed video."

GRADIUM(TM) glass, an optical quality glass with internal light-bending properties, reduces the optical aberrations typical in lenses made of conventional glass. GRADIUM(TM) lenses streamline the functions performed by conventional lens systems. LightPath has 10 patents, and several more pending, on the process to make GRADIUM(TM) glass.
